definitions.gloss: sociable; good at keeping company; willing to go along with others
definitions.explanation: Describes someone who readily joins social activities, accepts invitations, and is easy to spend time with. Highly valued in Japanese workplace and social culture.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{付|つ}き{合|あ}いがいい{人|ひと}だ。
{飲|の}みに{誘|さそ}うといつも{来|く}てくれて、{付|つ}き{合|あ}いがいい。
examples.english: He always comes when invited for drinks — he's good company.

examples.japanese: {付|つ}き{合|あ}いがいいのはいいが、{自分|じぶん}の{時間|じかん}も{大切|たいせつ}にしたほうがいい。
examples.english: Being sociable is fine, but you should also value your own time.

notes:
USAGE:
A compliment in Japanese social culture, where willingness to join group activities (especially after-work drinking) is valued. The opposite is {付|つ}き{合|あ}いが{悪|わる}い (unsociable, reluctant to join). The noun {付|つ}き{合|あ}い alone means "social relations" or "company."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {付|つ}き{合|あ}いがいい{人|ひと} (a sociable person)
- {付|つ}き{合|あ}いが{悪|わる}い (unsociable; a poor sport about joining in)
- {付|つ}き{合|あ}いで{飲|の}む (to drink to be sociable)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese workplace culture, {付|つ}き{合|あ}い (social obligation/keeping company) is an important concept. Being {付|つ}き{合|あ}いがいい helps build relationships, while being {付|つ}き{合|あ}いが{悪|わる}い can be seen as standoffish.
